Farm Implements and Machinery Sectional Committee. FAD 59 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard (Part 2) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the 
Farm Implements and Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division 
Council. 

Removal of stalks by pulling by hand is very difficult and time consuming. For this purpose stalk pullers have 
been developed and are being used. Considering the use of stalk puller for pulling out the stalks of lantena 
species In the forest, a need was felt to prepare this standard for helping in quality production of this tool. 

While Part 1 of this standard covers the requirements of light duty stalk puller, this Part 2 covers the requirements 
of heavy duty stalk puller. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 *Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)*. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 13485 (Pwt2):19W 

Indian Standard 

FORESTRY TOOLS — STALK PULLER — 
SPECinCATION 

PART 2 HEAVY DUTY 



1 SCOPE 

This standard (Part 2) specifics the materials, 
dimensions and other requirements for Stalk Puller, 
heavy duty used for uprooting congested bushes such 
as lantena, etc. 

2 REFERENCES 

The Indian Standards as given below contain 
provisions which through reference in this text, 
constitute provision of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most recent 
editions of the standards indicated below:

3 MATERIALS 

3.1 Various components ofStalk Puller shall be made 
from materials given below: 

Component Materials 

Tongue Nfild steel (see IS 2062) 

Wheel Hafdrubba'(soUd) 

Knurling plate High carbon steel (see IS 2507) 

Handles Steel tube (see IS 3601) 

4 SHAPE AND IHMENSIONS 

4.1 The dimensions of heavy duty Stalk PuHer shall 
be as given in Fig. 1. 



4.2 The tolerances on various dimensions shall be of 
coarse class specified in IS 2102 (Part 1). 

5 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Knurling shall be provided on tongue and stay as 
shown in Fig. 1 so that there is proper gripping and 
holding of bushes. 

SJ2 Wheels shall be free and Stalk Puller shall move 
on these wheels freely and smoothly. 

S3 Fukrum shall free from any play. 

5.4 The jaws shall have a minimum opening of 100 
mm. 

5^ The weight of heavy duty stalk puller shall not 
exceed 40 kilograms. 

6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 The entire surface of the Stalk Puller except the 
knurling on the jaws shall be smooth. 

6J The Stalk Puller shall be free fnxn (kfects, such 
as cracks, rusts, burrs and other manufacturing defects. 

6u3 All sharp comers shall be rounded olf . 

6.4 The steel pipe, if used for handle, etc, shall ^ 
galvanized or painted widi rust-prevemive coatinp. 
Other steel components shall be painted with rust- 
preventive coatings. 

<L5 The welding shall not be porous. 

6.6 All ni^ and bdts shall be securely tigbtened and 
wheel axle and fulcrum shall be ptoperiy lubncaled. 

7 PERF0RMAN€::E TEST 

An assembled puller shall be placed on a hocizoatal 
surface and operated for at least 25 times, to obs^ve 
the smooth opening and closing of the jaws. 

8 DESIGNATION 

The designation shall incliKk the type of the stalk 
puller and the number of this Indian Standard as: 

Stalk PiiUc?, Heavy Duty, IS 13485 (Part 2)

c\ Batch. Code or Serial Number; and 
d) Type. 

9.2 BIS CertillaitkMi Marking

10 PACiONG 

The Stalk Puller shall be suitably packed to avoid 
damage in handling and transport
